title: The Violet Line: A Consent Ledger of Affected Parties
description: A consent-ledger instrument for projects. It maintains a ledger of the parties a project affects and what they actually recorded at a review date; absence of consent is recorded — the UNRECORDED state — never inferred from silence, absence, or convenience. An executable review returns one of three verdicts (ACCOUNTED, UNACCOUNTED, OUT_OF_SCOPE); an ACCOUNTED reading never authorizes an action, a release, or a use outside the scope a party named. Subtitle: Absence of consent recorded, never inferred Apache-2.0 licensed; see LICENSE in the repository.

methods.name: Per-project consent ledger with four recorded states
methods.description: Defines a ledger of (party, state, scope, date) records where absence of consent is represented only by an explicit UNRECORDED state.
methods.evidence: The ledger records four states: CONSENTED, DECLINED, WITHDRAWN, and UNRECORDED Definition 1.

methods.name: Staged, fail-closed intake with set-aside codes
methods.description: Intake dispositions every submitted record as KEPT or one of four set-aside codes with a preserving note, never dropping or inventing states.
methods.evidence: Intake first dispositions every submitted record: KEPT, or one of four set-aside codes (malformed, unreadable date, future date, unknown state), each carrying a note that preserves the submission Definition 3.

methods.name: Tag-matched rule registry producing three verdicts
methods.description: Versioned consent rules are matched to projects by declared tags and scored against the kept ledger to yield ACCOUNTED, UNACCOUNTED, or OUT_OF_SCOPE.
methods.evidence: Rules are then matched to the project by declared tags and scored against the kept ledger Definition 2. A rule is ACCOUNTED only when the kept ledger holds the states it requires

methods.name: Formal definitions and propositions bound to tests
methods.description: States the instrument's behaviour as definitions and propositions (non-permission, fail-closed, declines persist, scope travels) linked to a claim-ledger test.
methods.evidence: All formalism references in this manuscript resolve to blocks declared in 03b_formalism.md and are bound by tests/test_form alism_claim_ledger.py through data/formalism_claim_ledger.json.

methods.name: Worked example reviews
methods.description: Illustrates behaviour with a community interview study, a fully set-aside submission, and an out-of-scope project.
methods.evidence: A community interview study declares tags research and community and submits two records: interviewees CONSENTED with scope “quoted, named”, and a moderator UNRECORDED.

key_findings: In the worked interview example, one UNRECORDED moderator entry causes the review to return UNACCOUNTED, with absence recorded rather than inferred.
Empty, fully set-aside, or unscorable inputs return UNACCOUNTED with a note rather than raising an exception or a fabricated value.
No verdict, including ACCOUNTED, grants or implies permission; it describes ledger coverage only.
The author notes the instrument cannot verify that a recorded state was given honestly, freely, or recently, and that ACCOUNTED is coverage, not safety.
key_findings_evidence: The review keeps both records, applies the naming, recording, and decline rules, and returns UNACCOUNTED with reasons naming the UNRECORDED entry. Absence is recorded; nothing is inferred.

For every empty or fully set-aside scan set, and for every unscorable registry, the review returns UNACCOUNTED with an explanatory note and zero findings; no path raises an exception or returns a fabricated value.
No verdict grants, implies, or encodes permission.
It cannot verify that a recorded state was given honestly, freely, or recently. • ACCOUNTED is coverage, not safety: a complete ledger of coerced consent is still complete.
